correctness.rationale: Reflecting k black coordinates maps Ferroni minimal-matroid bases isometrically to conv(0,{e_i+f_j}) in H:sum y=sum z=s; an explicit product decomposition with weights y_i z_j/s proves the full halfspace system y_i,z_j>=0 and s<=1. The intrinsic projected normal norms are h=sqrt((n-1)/n) for coordinates and b=sqrt(kr/n) for the base facet. Clearance constraints y_i,z_j>=h rho and s+b rho<=1 give rho<=1/(max(k,r)h+b), attained by feasible centers. At equality the max-size group coordinates are fixed to h rho while the other group surplus is an arbitrary nonnegative vector of sum |k-r| h rho; hence full center locus a regular simplex dimension min(k,r)-1 except rank=corank gives unique point. Tangency and fixed-n maximum floor((n-3)/2) follow. An independent scipy linear-program check for all 2<=k,r<=7 matched the analytic radius, but algebra proves the unrestricted statement.
